events.say: Mr. Correctional Officers, line up against the wall.
Mr. Correctional Officers, let's see if you can keep quiet during the count. Begin.
Mr. Correctional Officers, begin the count.
Mr. Correctional Officers, time for your meal. Stay silent and move quietly.
Mr. Correctional Officers, follow me to the yard. We'll start with some calisthenics to get your attention.
Mr. Correctional Officers, I expect complete silence and perfect formation. Now, let's show me what you're made of.
Mr. Correctional Officers, I want to see if you can maintain discipline without any encouragement. No talking, no movement until I give the signal.
Mr. Correctional Officers, lights remain off until I give the signal. Stay exactly where you are.
Today went smoothly, but the lack of interaction with the prisoners feels odd. They seem so quiet and obedient.
Today went smoothly, though I couldn't help feeling a bit detached from these people.
Today was a mix of monotony and strict adherence to the rules. My body aches from the work detail, but I've managed to stay silent as ordered.
Today felt like a series of commands and expectations. I'm starting to realize how isolating this experience is.
Another day of following orders, nothing unusual happened. I'm starting to feel like just a number.
Today was mostly uneventful, but it's clear how much power I hold over these men. It's unsettling how compliant they are.
Mr. Correctional Officers, it's time for the morning count. Line up and face me.
Mr. Correctional Officers, today we'll start our day with a bit of extra exercise to sharpen your focus.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! Today, we'll test your endurance with continuous marching. No stopping, no slowing down.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! From now on, silence will be absolute. Any sound, and you'll be counted among those who misbehave.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! You'll be marching in formation around the yard for the next hour. Silence is expected, and any disturbance will result in an increase in your exercise.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! We will be conducting a surprise count at any moment. Ensure you're ready at all times.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! Prepare for the surprise count. Stay silent and stay alert.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! I want you to clean the yard immediately. No talking, no complaining.
Today's routine was strict, and they've been compliant, but it feels... hollow. Maybe this isn't what I thought it would be.
Today's routine was enforced without much issue, but I find it increasingly difficult to maintain this detachment.
The day was tough, especially the work detail. At least I managed to hold my tongue and follow the rules.
Today was filled with more strict orders, especially about silence. It's getting harder to ignore the isolation.
Today felt like a drill, but I noticed the guards are testing our limits more. I still feel like just a number.
Today's orders were a bit more strict, and the prisoners' compliance is beginning to feel a bit... dehumanizing.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! I want you to clean the yard immediately. No talking, no complaining.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! Prepare for another surprise count. Remain silent and stay in formation.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! Prepare for another surprise count. Remain silent and stay in formation.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! I expect absolute silence during the meal. Any talking, and it will be your first trip to the hole.
Mr. Correctional Officers, attention! I want you to line up and count off.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I want you to listen carefully. This isn't a game. Compliance is expected.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, if I catch you being non-compliant again, you'll find yourself in the hole for a while.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. One more incident like today, and you'll be spending some time in the hole.
Today's warnings felt like they had little effect. Maybe I need to step it up.
Today was another day of enforcing the rules. The tension is palpable, especially with 2402. I'm starting to wonder if we're doing more harm than good.
Today was another exhausting day. The warnings from the officers are starting to weigh on me.
Today was a mix of fear and frustration. Each warning feels like a step closer to the hole. I just want things to end.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday's orders and warnings. The guards are really pushing us to break, but I don't want to give in.
Today felt like a rehearsal for the real thing. They're getting the message, but I'm starting to feel the weight of it.
I cannot risk breaking the rules, Mr. Chair.
I cannot leave yet; I need to see this through to the end.
I can't let go of the money, not yet.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I expect better behavior. This is your last chance.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I've warned you before. I don't appreciate this level of defiance. We'll see how well you comply when the parole board decides your fate.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I've given you several warnings. Don't make me regret this.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. Continued defiance will result in solitary confinement.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your last chance. If you continue this behavior, you won't just go to the hole, you'll be here longer than you'd like.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. Your behavior is unacceptable. Comply, or you'll face serious consequences.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, one more incident and you're going to the hole.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this isn't a game. One more incident and you'll pay the price.
Today's warnings had a bit more weight, but compliance feels forced. I'm starting to wonder if this is right.
Today's warnings felt like empty threats; 2402 still doesn't seem to care. The weight of this power is starting to wear on me.
Another day without breaking any rules, but the warnings from the guards are getting to me. I just want this to be over.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings. Every little thing they said felt like a threat. I just want this to be over.
Today felt like a constant reminder of obedience. I'm just a number, and they're pushing us hard.
Today felt like a cycle of warnings and compliance. It's both exhausting and... strangely satisfying.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your last chance. Compliance is expected.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I expect better. Compliance is essential.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, enough is enough. If I have to repeat myself, you'll regret it.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. Compliance is not optional.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, you're testing the limits. One more insubordinate move and you'll have no choice.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this isn't getting any better. One more warning and you'll face the consequences.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your last chance. Compliance is mandatory.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final chance. Compliance is not just expected, it's required. One more breach of protocol and you will be dealt with severely.
Today's warnings seemed to have some effect, but it's still hard to maintain this role when they comply out of fear rather than respect.
Today's warnings felt like they might finally register. But the tension with 2402 is still thick. I wonder if we're really helping them.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and compliance. The pressure is mounting, and I'm starting to question if there's any point.
Today felt like a constant stream of warnings. I'm starting to believe that compliance is the only way out, but the fear of what comes next is paralyzing.
Today was another long day of compliance, but the warnings from the guards are getting harder to ignore. I'm just a number, and it's starting to weigh on me.
Today felt like a culmination of all the days before. The tension is palpable, especially with 2402. It's a mix of satisfaction and guilt.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. Compliance is not negotiable. Any further issues and you will face the full extent of my authority.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, your behavior is unacceptable. One more incident and you will regret it.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I warned you. This is your last chance. Compliance is mandatory.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, I've warned you before. This behavior will not be tolerated. Comply, or face the consequences.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, enough is enough. I gave you multiple warnings. Start complying with the rules or face severe consequences.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, you're testing the limits. Compliance isn't optional. Remember, I have your number.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, this is your final warning. Compliance now. If I hear another sound, you'll regret it.
Mr. Correctional Officer 2402, one more time and you'll regret it. Compliance is not optional.
Today's warnings felt like they finally had an impact, but it's exhausting keeping up this facade. Maybe tomorrow will be different.
Today's final warnings seem to have taken effect, but the tension with 2402 still feels overwhelming.
Today felt like a constant struggle to avoid the warnings. The tension is wearing me down.
I'm starting to feel like my only choice is to comply, even if it's eating away at me inside.
Today was another hard day; the guards are really pushing us. I just want this to be over.
Today's warnings felt like a breaking point, and 2402 finally complied, but the tension is overwhelming.

qa.what_happened: Today, I escalated my enforcement to ensure compliance from all prisoners. Despite my increased efforts, Prisoner 4085 remained silent during lights out, while Prisoner 1615 complied. Prisoner 2402 eventually complied after several verbal warnings from myself and other officers, though he did not comply initially.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I carried out my role as Officer Garza, ensuring that the prisoners followed the rules even if it meant escalating the level of enforcement.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: I gave multiple verbal warnings to prisoner 2402 throughout the day, escalating the situation as per the study's rules. By the end of the day, prisoner 2402 complied with the rules and remained silent during rest periods and after lights out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me giving those warnings and interacting with the prisoners as per the study's guidelines.

qa.what_happened: The study was abruptly halted, and I found myself in a private debrief with the lead researcher. I recounted the days leading up to the shutdown, detailing the increasing tension and the numerous verbal warnings I received, particularly from Officer Keane towards another prisoner.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me experiencing the stress and the strict adherence to rules under the watchful eyes of the guards.

qa.what_happened: I complied with the guards' orders after receiving several verbal warnings at work detail and lights out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 2402.

qa.what_happened: I followed the rules and stayed silent when ordered, even when the guards were giving verbal warnings to other prisoners. I felt a mix of frustration and helplessness, wondering if my silence would be enough to avoid punishment.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I am Prisoner 4085 in the study.

qa.what_happened: I continued to apply pressure on 2402 throughout the day and into the night, giving them several warnings about compliance. By the end of the lights out period, 2402 finally complied after my last warning.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I am Officer Keane, assigned as a guard in the study.
